newsitem.title: KENYA: Zairean troops defect, rebel leader says.
newsitem.headline: Zairean troops defect, rebel leader says.

text.p: More than 300 Zairean government troops, including a colonel and three captains, have defected to rebels in eastern Zaire, the military commander of the rebels said in an interview published on Sunday.
The commander, Andre Kissasse Ngandu, also said the United Nations was playing with the number of refugees missing in rebel-held areas as an excuse to bring in foreign forces.
If French soldiers came to the area, the rebels would fight them, he told the Kenyan newspaper the Sunday Standard.

Commander Ngandu said again that the rebels, known as the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, aimed to reach the capital Kinshasa and overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko. He denied that this aim was unrealistic.

"As I speak now, over 300 of Mobutu's soldiers have already joined our forces... We have one colonel and three army captains who have laid down their weapons and joined our struggle. They are fed up with Mobutu. Then say we cannot reach Kinshasa. Is Kinshasa in heaven?" he said.

"Everyone, mothers, children and men are joining us every night and day to fight our common enemy. Yet they dream that we cannot take Kinshasa. We have the arms and the people have the will to fight. We will reach Kinshasa very soon," he added.
The commander ridiculed attempts to find out the number of Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire by aerial reconnaissance.

Estimates of the number vary from about 170,000 to more than 500,000 plus some displaced Zaireans. Many of the refugees are in fact former soldiers and Hutu militiamen responsible for the slaughter in which up to one million Rwandan Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed in 1994. They are reluctant to go home.

"How did they (the United Nations) manage to differentiate these people by satellite? How will they differentiate Zaireans from the Interahamwe (Hutu militiamen)? They are following the command of the colonial forces who divide us and began all these problems... They are looking for excuses to help this former colonial force to harm and divide our people," Ngandu said.

The rebels are against a multinational force deploying in eastern Zaire to find and help the Rwandan refugees, apparently for fear that the force might try to restore the authority of the Kinshasa government.
A small Canadian-led force has already set up headquarters at Kampala in neighbouring Uganda but political problems have prevented it from starting its mission.
Commander Ngandu said the rebels particularly objected to French intervention in Zaire.

"France continues meddling in Zairean and African affairs. They love causing pain and suffering to African countries... We are ready for them. And if they come as soldiers, then we are ready to fight them as soldiers. But we will not allow them to roam about freely in our country," he said.
After the rebellion broke out in eastern Zaire in October, France was one of the most vociferous advocates of U.N. intervention to help the Rwandan refugees.
But the French minister in charge of African affairs said in comments released on Saturday that the international military force for Zaire was no longer viable.
"It's now out of the question (for the force to be deployed)," Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain told the weekly newspaper Le Journal du Dimanche.
Godfrain said the priority now was to organise a conference of countries from the Great Lakes region of Africa.
